solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Zesty thing, failure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sharp citrus fruit whose peel gives zest
second meaning: slang for a dud, something that does not work

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate meanings of one word, with only a comma between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus fruit is the zesty thing, and in slang a useless car or product is called by the same fruit's name.

clue.text: Cuckoo caught by buffalo, comfortably

indicators.note: the answer is trapped inside the following words, held across the gap between them

parts.note: the end of buffalo runs into the start of comfortably

explanation.surface: A cuckoo perched snugly on a buffalo's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is informal Spanish-derived slang for crazy, and cuckoo is another informal word for mad.

clue.text: Dog leads on many, unlikely terriers tethered

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters, so take the first letter of each word that follows

parts.note: the initials of the four words

explanation.surface: A dog-walker holds many leashes, though terriers are rarely kept tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutt is an informal word for a dog, especially a mongrel of mixed breed.

clue.text: Remake has rotten direction

indicators.note: to remake something is to build it again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict that a film remake has gone badly off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' reads as film-making beside 'Remake', but it means a compass heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Northeast is a compass point, one of the bearings a traveller can head in.

clue.text: Bright star seen in April, so extraordinary

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stargazer remarks how unusually bright a star looks this April.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the Pole Star or North Star, is a bright star in the constellation Ursa Minor.

clue.text: Spread covering Irish Rover

indicators.note: one thing covering another wraps round it, so the first piece goes outside the second

parts.note: pâté is a savoury spread for toast
IR is the standard abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Butter spread over an Irish setter called Rover, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' looks like a dog's name or a wanderer; here it is the old word for a sea robber.
explanation.definitionFit: Rover is an archaic term for a pirate, a sea raider who roves the seas plundering ships.

clue.text: Books on fire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short form of literature

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a book-burning; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit is short for literature, a body of written works, and it is also the past participle of light, meaning set alight.

clue.text: Telling tale, grin maniacally

indicators.note: acting maniacally means wildly and out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a story while grinning like a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate it, so relating is a synonym of telling in that sense.

clue.text: Newspaper airs bits and bobs

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to air laundry is to dry it

explanation.surface: A newspaper broadcasts odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airs' suggests broadcasting alongside a newspaper, but it means drying out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small items, which is what the British idiom bits and bobs describes.

clue.text: Deliverer of food in rebuilt terrace

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again differently, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A food delivery to a renovated terraced house.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies and serves meals for events, so is a provider who brings food to people.

clue.text: Eaglet ultimately has solitary short claw

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the final letter is dropped
ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the preceding word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the young eagle
being solitary means being on your own

explanation.surface: A young eagle in its nest with one stunted claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the sharp hooked claw of a bird of prey such as an eagle.

clue.text: Athlete blasted club

parts.note: a putter is a golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A sportsman curses his club, as with 'blasted club!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blasted' reads as a mild oath; it supplies a word meaning fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is a track-and-field athlete who throws the heavy metal ball.

clue.text: Complete cane broken: something to say?

indicators.note: something broken has its parts disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snapped walking stick: surely that deserves a comment?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning total; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is a spoken word or statement, literally a thing said aloud by someone.

clue.text: Sarnies organised with minimum of fuss, type without decoration

indicators.note: organising puts things into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written; sarnies is British slang for sandwiches

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest part, here just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Sandwiches arranged neatly without fuss, plain and undecorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sans serif is a typeface lacking serifs, the small decorative strokes at the ends of letter lines.

clue.text: Deliberate, one having finished absorbing religious books

indicators.note: something absorbing takes another thing into itself, so the following piece goes inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A careful person who has finished reading through scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Read one plus having finished as one piece, which then takes in the religious books.
explanation.definitionFit: Intended means done on purpose, the adjective sense of deliberate.

clue.text: Stop to pen a book

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it as in a sheep pen, so one piece shuts in the other

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or stop something officially

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop writing a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like writing but means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book published once a year, such as a children's yearly comic collection.

clue.text: Position held by Pakistan, certainly

indicators.note: the answer is held within the following words, straddling the gap between them

parts.note: the end of the country runs into the start of the adverb

explanation.surface: A diplomatic position that Pakistan definitely maintains.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is an attitude or standpoint taken on an issue, a synonym of position.

clue.text: Person having a flutter fully recovered

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gambler; a flutter is British slang for a small bet

explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is a small bet in British usage; the surface hints at a heart flutter, making a recovery seem medical.
explanation.definitionFit: One who bets is a better, and someone well again after an illness is said to be better.

clue.text: Weather set to change, darling

indicators.note: these letters are set to change, so they will be rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A forecaster tells a loved one the weather is about to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetheart and darling are both terms of endearment for a loved one.

clue.text: Gelatinous substance a scrap of cloth picked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a scrap of cloth smeared with jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly-like substance from seaweed, used for culturing microbes and as a food thickener.

clue.text: Cut the new bandages carefully at first

indicators.note: bandages wrap round a wound, so the first piece wraps around the next
new suggests a fresh version, so the preceding letters take a different order
at first means the beginning, so only the initial letter of the preceding word is used

explanation.surface: A cut that the new dressing must cover with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' sits with bandages to suggest a wound, but it means engrave.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into a surface, as with acid on metal or a tool on glass.

clue.text: Broadcaster in South American city screening commercial

indicators.note: a screen shields what is behind it, so the city surrounds the next piece

explanation.surface: A broadcaster in Rio showing a commercial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screening' in a TV surface suggests showing, but it means hiding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is a medium that transmits programmes over the airwaves, so it broadcasts.

clue.text: Bird on wall at regular intervals

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one, skipping those in between

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A bird perching on a wall every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: The owl is a nocturnal bird of prey, so a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: Snug clothes on in the near future

indicators.note: used as a verb, clothes means dresses or covers, so one piece wraps the other

explanation.surface: Close-fitting clothes will be worn later today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as a noun, but it is a verb meaning covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight means this coming evening, a time that is soon to arrive.

clue.text: Tinkerer, one taking a bow?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who fiddles about with things
second meaning: a violinist, who draws a bow across the strings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a bow' suggests a performer acknowledging applause; the question mark flags the bow as the violin's.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin player handles a bow, and someone who tinkers aimlessly is said to fiddle about.

clue.text: World having change of heart

indicators.note: a change of something alters its arrangement, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: The whole world has a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' is an idiom for a new opinion; here it literally rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is our planet, the world on which we live.
